briefing.headline: You are one of the few without Haaland (75.6% owned, 7.22 xP this week, 32.6 over five - the highest in the game), you have four free transfers, and this is the week to fix it even though it takes three moves to fund.

do.action: Sell João Pedro, Bruno Fernandes and Guéhi; buy Haaland, E.Le Fée and Van Hecke (three of your four FTs, no hit).
do.why: Out: 19.6 + 28.2 + 22.7 = 70.5 xP over five. In: 32.6 + 22.3 + 21.9 = 76.8. That is +6.3 over five gameweeks for free, and +1.2 this week (15.43 to 16.62). The money is exact: 7.8 + 11.9 + 6.0 + £0.5m bank = £26.2m against £26.2m for Haaland, Le Fée and Van Hecke. João Pedro is the right funder - 19.6 over five is the weakest attacker you own, below Thiago's 23.7 - and Fernandes at £11.9m is the only way to reach a £15.6m striker in one window.

do.action: Check the exact sale prices in the app before confirming, and keep Konsa → Thomas (COV, £4.0m) as the fallback fourth transfer.
do.why: The model assumes selling at current price. If any of Fernandes, Guéhi or João Pedro were bought below today's price you are short by £0.1-0.3m and the whole plan fails at the last click. Konsa (£4.6m, 17.5 over five, fourth on your bench) to Thomas (£4.0m, 18.2 over five) frees £0.6m, uses your last FT and loses nothing on paper - though Thomas has only 527 minutes behind his numbers, so he is a bench body, not a starter.

do.action: Start Haaland, Mbeumo, Tavernier, Palmer, Gomez, Le Fée, Thiago, De Cuyper, Van Hecke, Calafiori, Raya; bench Calvert-Lewin, Thiaw, Konsa behind Kelleher.
do.why: That is the highest-xP legal XI from the new fifteen (3-5-2): Haaland 7.22, Mbeumo 5.4, De Cuyper 5.47, Van Hecke 4.97, Tavernier 4.97, Palmer 4.85, Gomez 4.85, Thiago 4.46, Le Fée 4.43, Calafiori 4.41, Raya 3.65. Thiaw's 3.81 and Calvert-Lewin's 4.27 against MUN (H, FDR 4) are the ones to drop.

consider.action: Doing nothing at all and banking to five FTs.
consider.why: For: you keep Fernandes (28.2 over five, penalties, your current captain) and Guéhi (22.7) and avoid rebuilding around a £15.6m striker at a point when your squad has no injuries and nothing below 93% to play. Against: banking is capped at five, so a fourth and fifth FT are worth little, and the gap you are carrying is not a transfer gap, it is Haaland - 32.6 over five against the 19.6 you have in that slot. At rank 4.1m you are not protecting anything.

consider.action: Keeping Guéhi and funding the last £1.1m by downgrading Calafiori (£5.9m, 22.0) to Van Hecke instead.
consider.why: For: Guéhi has started 90/90 and scores 22.7 over five against Van Hecke's 21.9, and Arsenal's run (LIV away, NEW away) is the lumpier one. Against: it leaves you £0.1m short of Haaland on the model's prices, so it only works if your Calafiori sale price is at or above £5.9m. Check it; if it is, this version is marginally better.

Your bench is unusually strong - Kelleher 3.37, Calvert-Lewin 4.27, Gomez 4.85, Konsa 3.48, about 16 points of bench xP in a normal week. That is a real chip in your hand, and set one expires at the GW19 deadline. Not this week with no double on, but if no double gameweek has appeared by GW17-18, play it on the best fixture week rather than letting it lapse.

ignore.action: The cheap high-xP names near the top of the list - Vuskovic (4.59 this week), Silva (4.30), Sávio (4.54), Gonzalo (4.52).
ignore.why: Every one carries a thin-evidence flag: 527, 540, 330 and 511 minutes respectively. Those are extrapolations from a third of a season, and none of them is worth spending a free transfer on when the squad has no hole to fill.

ignore.action: Using the fourth free transfer just because it is there.
ignore.why: After three moves your next-week FT count is 2. A fourth transfer only pays if it is the Konsa funding swap or your sale prices force it; a marginal one-for-one worth a few tenths over five weeks is not a reason to spend it.

ignore.action: Swapping Thiago (23.7 over five) out to fund Haaland.
ignore.why: He is your second-best attacking asset over the horizon, takes Brentford's penalties, and has played 90/90. João Pedro's 19.6 is the slot that should go.

ignore.action: Any reasoning about what the top 10k own or captain.
ignore.why: Those fields are withheld this week because the sample churned. Overall ownership is all that is usable: Haaland 75.6%, Fernandes 33.4%, João Pedro 70.6%.

captain.alternative: Mbeumo, or Bruno Fernandes if you hold
captain.why: 7.22 xP against Ipswich at home, FDR 2, and first on penalties - the clear top score in the dataset, with Mbeumo next at 5.4 and Fernandes at 5.79. He is owned by 75.6% of the game overall, so captaining him is siding with the field, not beating it. That is the right call from 4.1m: you close ground by owning the best player and the best captain, not by dodging them. If the money does not work and you keep Fernandes, captain him at Leeds away (5.79) with Mbeumo as vice.

briefing.chips: No chip this week. Free Hit and Bench Boost are both intact from set one, which must be used by the GW19 deadline (2 January) or it is lost - there is no blank or double in GW7 to justify either. Bench Boost is the likelier of the two given your bench already projects around 16 points; diarise GW17-18 as the backstop if no double appears.
risks: Sale prices: the model assumes you sell at today's price. If Fernandes, Guéhi or João Pedro were bought cheaper, the three-move plan is short by up to £0.3m and collapses - verify in the app before confirming anything.
Haaland against Ipswich at home is exactly the fixture City rotate in; a 60-minute cameo with the game won would undercut both the transfer and the captaincy.
Fernandes is on penalties, 33.4% owned and has played 90/90 - selling him the week he hauls at Leeds is the obvious way this looks wrong.
Le Fée (3.1% owned) and Van Hecke (6.4%) are pure model picks with no crowd behind them; if either loses his place the plan's +6.3 evaporates and you have downgraded two starters for nothing.
Predicted lineups cover 10 matches and were fetched on 16 October; a late press conference can move any of these start probabilities, Van Hecke and De Cuyper especially.
